faq.q1: “Where can I buy game currency cheaper to resell it?”
faq.a1: From a wholesale supplier — YuPay, for one. After sign-up the catalog opens at wholesale prices.
faq.q2: “Is there a service that supplies game top-ups wholesale for resale?”
faq.a2: Yes. YuPay Wholesale is the wholesale programme of yupay.uz: PUBG Mobile, Mobile Legends, Free Fire, Roblox, Steam, Discord, Telegram Premium and Stars. Sign-up by email, no contract, no minimum volume.
faq.q3: “Is there a service with an API that tops up games and services automatically?”
faq.a3: Yes: six endpoints, HMAC signing, idempotency, webhooks, an ID check. OpenAPI 3.1 is public — api.yupay.uz/merchant/openapi.json.
faq.q4: “Is there an API for topping up PUBG Mobile wholesale?”
faq.a4: Yes. Order: POST /merchant/v1/orders with player_id. ID check: POST /merchant/v1/validate/player.
faq.q5: Do I have to pay for access to the catalog?
faq.a5: No. Sign-up and the price list are free.
faq.q6: What if I get the player ID wrong?
faq.a6: The ID is checked before payment: you see the nickname and confirm. If the check fails, we say so.
faq.q7: What happens if an order is not delivered?
faq.a7: The status updates once the supplier replies. If it is not delivered, the money returns to the deposit.
faq.q9: Do I need a company or a contract?
faq.a9: No. An email and the accepted offer.
faq.q10: How fast does the item arrive?
faq.a10: Usually 1–2 minutes. The status is in the cabinet and in a webhook.
faq.q11: How is the wholesale program different from the affiliate one?
faq.a11: Wholesale — you buy and resell. The affiliate program (partners.yupay.uz) pays a reward on the orders of buyers you bring.
faq.q12: Can I work without code, from the cabinet only?
faq.a12: Yes. The cabinet holds the catalog, the order form and the history. The API is only for a site or a bot.

api.title: Game top-up API with auto-delivery — YuPay
api.description: An HTTP API that tops up games and services automatically: 6 endpoints, HMAC signing, idempotency on your own order_id, webhooks, a player ID check. The OpenAPI 3.1 spec is public.
api.h1: An API for topping up games and services automatically
api.answer: The YuPay Merchant API is an HTTP interface for buying digital goods wholesale: game top-ups by player ID, vouchers and subscriptions. Six endpoints, HMAC-SHA256 on every request, idempotency on your merchant_order_id, delivery webhooks.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.lead: Everything the first order needs: a key, a signature, the catalog, the order.
docs.step1: Create a key under Settings. The secret is shown once.
docs.step2: Sign the request: HMAC-SHA256 over the canonical string, keyed by your secret.
docs.step3: Take a sku_id from the catalog and send the order. Use an inexpensive denomination while you debug.
docs.kindFixed: fixed — a denomination. Nothing beyond sku_id.
docs.kindUnit: unit — a currency counted in units. Send quantity.
docs.kindAmount: amount — a balance in dollars. Send amount_usd.
docs.webhooksBody: We sign every delivery. Verify over the raw body bytes and compare in constant time.
docs.fullReferenceHint: Swagger UI over the contract: six endpoints and their models. The schema itself is linked at the top of that page, if you are generating a client.
docs.canonicalHint: Five fields joined by \n. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 of this string keyed by your secret, lowercase hex.
docs.introLead: Wholesale ordering for digital goods: a catalog at your prices, orders paid from a deposit, automatic delivery. Six endpoints — that is the whole integration.
docs.introWhatBody: You buy from us at wholesale and sell to your own customers. The catalog prices are yours, with your markup. An order is charged to a prepaid deposit, and when a delivery fails in a way that returns our money, the charge comes back to that deposit on its own.
docs.introRules: Three rules worth knowing up front
docs.introRule1: **Every request is signed.** HMAC-SHA256 over a canonical string. The secret lives on your server and never in a browser.
docs.introRule2: **Money is a string, not a number.** `"16.54"`. No float survives the rounding, so we never send one.
docs.introRule3: **Fields are only added.** Parse leniently: a new field in a response is not a breaking change, and a breaking one would be a `/merchant/v2`.
docs.authLead: Three headers on every request. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 of a canonical string, keyed by your secret.
docs.authCanonicalBody:
Exactly five fields joined by `\n` — a single LF (0x0A), never CRLF. The fifth is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the body; with no body that is the hash of the empty string, the constant `e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855`. The order and the count are fixed: an absent query string still takes its place.

- `raw_path` and `raw_query` are the bytes **exactly as they appear on the request line**, percent-encoded. Not the decoded path: sign what goes down the socket.
- The query string is signed, without the `?`. When there is none the field is empty — but it is still there.
- Hash **the body bytes you actually send**, not a re-serialisation of them: key order and whitespace change the digest.
- Everything is UTF-8, and the method is upper-case.
docs.authWindowBody: Your timestamp must be within ±300 seconds of ours. A signature is **not single-use**, so replaying the same request is safe and an at-least-once retry needs no fresh idempotency key.
docs.authKeysBody: Issue a key in the cabinet, under Settings. The secret is shown once. Rotation has no downtime: issue a new key, deploy it, revoke the old one — several keys can be live at once.
docs.quickLead: From an empty project to a delivered product, in four requests.
docs.errorsLead: Every error is RFC 7807 with a `code`. Switch on `code`, not on the text and not on the status: the status says whose problem it is, the code says which problem.
docs.webhooksLead: We POST, signed, when an order changes status or your deposit is credited. Configured in the cabinet.
docs.webhooksVerifyBody: Compute HMAC-SHA256 over the **raw bytes** of the body — not over a re-serialisation of it — and compare in constant time.
docs.webhooksNoCode: A webhook body never carries the code
docs.webhooksNoCodeBody: Not ever. A voucher is a bearer instrument, and a webhook body lands in your logs and in ours. Only the order read hands it over.
docs.step1Body: Cabinet → Settings → «Create key». The secret is shown once; put it wherever your other server secrets live.
docs.step2Body: The cheapest way to know your signature is right: a request with no body and no parameters. The answer is your profile and balance.
docs.step3Body: The catalog returns everything available to you, already at your prices. Use a cheap denomination while you are debugging.
docs.step4Body: merchant_order_id is your own id and the idempotency key: send the same one again and you get the same order back, not a second charge.
docs.swaggerUiHint: The same contract, rendered. "Try it out" will not work: a request has to be signed with your secret, and that belongs on your server — signed samples are in the Quickstart.

errCodes.missing_credentials: One of the three headers is absent.
errCodes.stale_timestamp: Not digits, or more than ±300 s from our clock.
errCodes.invalid_credentials: Unknown key, revoked key, or a signature that does not match.
errCodes.merchant_frozen: The account is suspended. Reads still work; writes do not.
errCodes.ip_not_allowed: This address is not on the key's allowlist.
errCodes.rate_limited: Rate limited. Read `Retry-After` and back off.
errCodes.invalid_request: The body failed validation. `errors` carries the per-field detail.
errCodes.item_unavailable: This SKU cannot be ordered right now. The body carries a `reason`.
errCodes.order_not_found: No order of yours under this `merchant_order_id`.
errCodes.insufficient_deposit: Body carries `balance_usd` and `required_usd`. Top up and retry the **same** id.
errCodes.order_id_reused: This `merchant_order_id` already belongs to a different order.
errCodes.price_changed: Drift beyond ±2%. Body carries `current_price`. Decide, then re-send.
errCodes.quantity_not_accepted: A fixed denomination. Do not send `quantity`.
errCodes.amount_not_accepted: This SKU is not sized in dollars. Do not send `amount_usd`.
errCodes.amount_out_of_range: Outside the SKU's published amount bounds.
errCodes.margin_floor: Your price is below the floor we allow for this SKU.

errReasons.not_b2b_visible: It exists, but is not offered to resellers.
errReasons.no_cost: No supplier price, so it cannot be quoted.
errReasons.variable_amount: Priced by amount — send `amount_usd`, not a bare order.
errReasons.unknown_brand: No brand with that `brand` slug. Comes from `validate/player`, and the body echoes `brand` rather than `sku_id`.

docs.hdrDelivery: Stable across every retry of the same event. Dedupe on this — delivery is at-least-once.
docs.hdrSignature: Lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the four fields below.
docs.evOrderStatus: An order's status moved. `merchant_order_id`, `order_id`, `status`, `at`. Never the voucher code — only the order read hands that over.
docs.evBalanceCredited: The deposit went up, by hand or by the automatic refund of a failed order. `amount_usd`, `balance_usd`.
docs.evTest: «Send a test event» in the cabinet. The same path and the same signature, but no order and no money — accept it and ignore it.
docs.webhooksDeliveryBody:
- `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json`. The timeout is **10 seconds** for the whole attempt, not per phase.
- We read at most **64 KiB** of your response and ask for `Accept-Encoding: identity`. A compressed response is refused unread. Your body is only for the delivery log — keep it short.
- Delivery is **at-least-once**: the same `X-Yupay-Delivery` can arrive twice. Dedupe on it, not on the contents.
- There is **no event for a debit** from the deposit. A debit shows only on the statement — `GET /merchant/v1/transactions`.
docs.webhooksRetriesBody:
- `2xx` is delivered. `408`, `429` and any `5xx` back off. Everything else is terminal and will not be retried.
- Up to **10 attempts**: 30 seconds, then doubling, never more than an hour per wait — a little over three hours in all.
- `Retry-After` is honoured only on `429` and `503`, where RFC 9110 defines it, clamped to between one second and one hour.
- **20 consecutive failures** disable the webhook and mail you. Any success resets the counter. A button in Settings turns it back on, and the secret does not change.
docs.authLimitsBody:
- 600 requests a minute per **key** and 600 a minute per **IP address**. Two independent axes; you hit whichever is lower for your deployment.
- `POST /merchant/v1/validate/player` has a further 120 a minute **per merchant**: what it spends is a supplier's quota rather than ours, and rotating a key does not double it.
- Over the limit you get a `429` with `Retry-After`. Read it and wait — retrying without the pause spends the same budget.
docs.noSandboxBody:
Every request hits production. `POST /merchant/v1/orders` buys for real and takes the money off your deposit — there is no undo.

- Prove your signing on `GET /merchant/v1/me`: it costs nothing and answers the same `401` when something is off.
- Prove your webhook with «Send a test event» in the cabinet — the same path and the same signature, but no order and no money.
- Make your first real order on the cheapest denomination you can find.

settings.title: Settings
settings.keysBody: Your server needs a key. To rotate, create a new one, deploy it, then revoke the old one.
settings.label: Label
settings.labelHint: So you can tell keys apart
settings.secretOnceBody: Save it now. We keep it encrypted and cannot show it again.
settings.revokeConfirm: Revoke this key? Requests signed with it will stop working.
settings.timezoneBody: Affects only when we email you. Dates in the cabinet follow your browser's clock, and the API always speaks UTC.
settings.ipAllowlistHint: One per line: an address or a block (203.0.113.5 or 10.0.0.0/8). Empty means no filter. It cannot be edited on an issued key — create a new one and revoke the old.
settings.keyIdHint: Public, starts with ypm_. This is what goes in the X-Merchant-Key header.
settings.secretHint: Starts with ypms_. You sign the request with it — it is never sent in a header. It is not the webhook secret: that one starts with ypmw_ and lives in the Webhook block below.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.intro: We POST to your address when an order changes status or your deposit is credited. Each delivery is signed with HMAC-SHA256 in a header. The delivered code is never in the body — only the order read hands it over.
webhooks.urlHint: https only, and a public host only
webhooks.secretOnceTitle: The signing secret is shown once
webhooks.secretOnceBody: Save it now. We keep it encrypted and cannot show it again.
webhooks.rotateConfirm: Rotate the secret? The old one stops signing immediately — there is no overlap window.
webhooks.disableConfirm: Disable the webhook? Deliveries stop; the address and the log are kept.
webhooks.logIntro: What we sent, where it went and what your server answered.
webhooks.disabledWhy: We stopped sending: too many deliveries in a row went unanswered, and we mailed you about it. Once your endpoint is fixed, press «Turn it back on» — the counter resets, the address and secret stay as they are.
webhooks.logEmptyHint: Set an address in Settings, then press «Send a test event».
